ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the isosceles $\triangle ABC$ where $AB=AC$ and $\angle A<90^\circ$, $CD$ is the height of $\triangle ABC$, and $BE$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$, with $CD$ and $BE$ intersecting at point $P$. As the size of $\angle A$ changes, the shape of $\triangle EPC$ also changes. When $\angle A=36^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BPD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $AB=AC$ and $\angle A=36^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ABC=\angle ACB=\left(180-36\right)^\circ \div 2=72^\circ$,\\
since $CD\perp AB$,\\
thus $\angle BDC=90^\circ$,\\
given that $BE$ bisects $\angle ABC$,\\
hence $\angle ABE=\angle CBE=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABC=36^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle BPD=90^\circ-36^\circ=\boxed{54^\circ}$;
